answer: A skill I firmly believe everyone should have is basic cooking. In my view, it is a genuinely essential life skill that far too many people [[neglect]]. In Bangladesh, many young men grow up never having to cook, because mothers usually take care of the kitchen, and I was exactly the same until a few years ago. It is important because it directly affects your health, your finances and your independence. Relying entirely on takeaways and processed food is both expensive and unhealthy, whereas cooking allows you to eat well and [[affordably]]. This is especially relevant for students going abroad, and I always tell the students I advise to learn a few dishes before they leave. People can learn it easily these days, with countless free tutorials available online, so there really is no excuse. Honestly, I think learning to cook is one of the most practical and [[empowering]] things a person can do. It gives you control over what you put into your body, and it means you are never stuck when you end up living on your own. Beyond the health benefits, I find cooking to be a surprisingly [[therapeutic]] and creative activity. I learned a few years ago, when my mother spent several weeks in the village looking after my grandparents, and she taught me the basics over the phone. Those weeks of burnt rice and oversalted dal were [[humbling]], but they transformed my daily life for the better. I genuinely believe that if everyone learned to cook a few simple meals, both public health and personal wellbeing would improve considerably.

followUps.q: What dish can you cook best?
followUps.answer: Probably chicken curry with rice. It took me many attempts to get the spices right, but now even my mother says it is quite good, which is high praise from her.

followUps.q: Should cooking be taught in schools?
followUps.answer: I think so, at least the basics. It would help both boys and girls become more independent, and it could also challenge the old idea that cooking is only a woman's [[responsibility]].

note: Persona fix: he learned from his mother (by phone while she cared for his grandparents) rather than purely self-taught; added gender-role context and advice to students going abroad; plain 'essential'/'practical' marks moved to [[neglect]] and [[empowering]], added [[humbling]].
